preference.competitive: at least one endpoint within two of best at either horizon, or B choice
preference.normalization: unit total pair weight per informative independent trajectory; mean over informative trajectories
preference.terminal: terminal children fixed production utility; exact raw/awarded WDL reported separately

protocol.selection: minimum development unregularized trajectory-mean loss including zero B; ties within 1e-12 favor smaller correction norm

games.simultaneous: two one-sided 97.5% pair-bootstrap lower bounds above .5
games.order: alternate candidate first color by opening; both budgets per opening

diagnostics.featureAblations: seven leave-one-feature-out corrections across all phases; no refit
diagnostics.rootAblationSubset: every fourth member of fixed 128 transfer IDs; depth six
diagnostics.exact: independent raw/awarded solver when at most ten empties; never infer exact early values
diagnostics.uncertainty: 10000 complete-source stratified bootstrap resamples by stratum/policy/search depth
diagnostics.rootGate: no mean D12 regret increase at depth six; depth four reported separately

protocol.pilotSchedule: one per 16 stratum/policy/depth cells plus eight complementary parity/turn cells; no assessment access
protocol.balance: exact stratum/policy/depth totals; within each cell occupied parity and turn counts differ by at most one
protocol.trajectory: random before occupied 12; thereafter B1/12% or B4/2%; complete to terminal
protocol.tie: row-major for full-window research alternatives; unchanged production search ties in timed play
protocol.forecast: sum cell-specific pilot maxima; no assumed parallel speedup above measured lower bound; full games use max measured pair cost per budget
protocol.locked: first session never queries assessment root/frontier or plays confirmation games

pauseReason: Full fixed experiment forecast exceeds scientific eight-hour ceiling at the actual pool size; no locked assessment opened

audit.cpuAccounting: Node process total includes worker threads; worker thread CPU is diagnostic, never added again. Native child CPU is separate.

workers.interpretation: A safe cap is an upper bound, not a count of running workers. Resource checks reduce the pool immediately; a later higher cap does not automatically increase it. A checkpoint/resume can restore the previously benchmarked count. Active tasks can be fewer than pool slots.
workers.fieldCaution: Progress.availableGiB is WSL available memory. Decisions use resource-history.limitingAvailableGiB, the minimum of Windows and WSL availability. The free-headroom threshold is a reserve, not measured worker consumption.

baselineTraining.interpretation: Descriptive training frontier choices only; D12 regret is estimated discs except independently solved parents. These are not fresh root-choice transfer results or evidence of learned playing strength.
